# Story 01 — Create Ticket

---

## Prerequisites

- **External:** `customers/create-customer` must be implemented first. This story assumes a `Customer` domain entity (id `Guid`) and a customer repository exist under `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/` and `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/`. If those are not yet present, coordinate with the owner of the customers feature slug before starting; do **not** stub a `Customer` entity from this story.
- Onion Architecture scaffolding is already in place (verified): `BaseEntity` at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Common/BaseEntity.cs`, `IGenericRepository<T>` at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Interfaces/IGenericRepository.cs`, `IUnitOfWork` at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Interfaces/IUnitOfWork.cs`, `ApplicationDbContext` at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/Context/ApplicationDbContext.cs`, `BaseApiController` at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Controllers/BaseApiController.cs`, `ValidationFilter` at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Filters/ValidationFilter.cs`.
- Authenticated staff role infrastructure exists (`Roles` constants at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Constants/Roles.cs`, JWT at `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Extensions/JwtAuthenticationExtensions.cs`).
- Frontend is out of scope for this story; the ticket-creation UI belongs to `agent-dashboard/*` stories and to `customer-portal/submit-ticket-via-customer-portal`.

---

## Story Goal

Introduce the **Ticket** aggregate as the core object of F02 Ticket Management, and expose an authenticated staff-side HTTP endpoint that creates a ticket for an existing customer.

In scope:

1. New `Ticket` domain entity (subject, description, status, customer FK, inherited audit from `BaseEntity`).
2. Initial status enum with a single seed value (e.g. `New`) — richer status transitions are `tickets/change-ticket-status`.
3. EF Core configuration + migration for the `Tickets` table.
4. Application-layer create command/handler with FluentValidation.
5. `POST /api/tickets` endpoint on a new `TicketsController`, restricted to staff roles.
6. Validation that the referenced `CustomerId` exists; otherwise a 404/validation-style rejection.

Explicitly **out of scope** (own stories): setting category/priority at creation, assignment, status transitions beyond the initial value, escalation, history/audit trail beyond `BaseEntity` audit fields, customer-portal submission flow, any frontend work.

```csharp
using CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Common;
using CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Enums;

namespace CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Entities;

/// <summary>
/// Aggregate root representing a customer support ticket. Category, priority,
/// assignment, and status transitions are handled by dedicated stories and are
/// intentionally absent from this initial shape.
/// </summary>
public class Ticket : BaseEntity
{
    public string Subject { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string? Description { get; set; }
    public TicketStatus Status { get; set; } = TicketStatus.New;

    // FK to Customer. Navigation deliberately not declared here to avoid a
    // hard reference before customers/create-customer lands its entity name;
    // add the navigation in a follow-up if/when Customer is finalized.
    public Guid CustomerId { get; set; }
}
```

- Keep the entity mutable-property style (no private setters / constructor validation) to match `ApplicationUser` and the other existing entities in this codebase.

### 2 — Infrastructure: EF configuration + DbSet + migration

Create file: `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/TicketConfiguration.cs`

```csharp
using CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Entities;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Metadata.Builders;

namespace CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure.Persistence.Configurations;

public class TicketConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<Ticket>
{
    public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<Ticket> builder)
    {
        builder.ToTable("Tickets");

        builder.HasKey(t => t.Id);

        builder.Property(t => t.Subject)
            .IsRequired()
            .HasMaxLength(200);

        builder.Property(t => t.Description)
            .HasMaxLength(4000);

        builder.Property(t => t.Status)
            .IsRequired()
            .HasConversion<int>();

        builder.Property(t => t.CustomerId)
            .IsRequired();

        builder.HasIndex(t => t.CustomerId);

        // Global soft-delete filter (matches project-wide convention on BaseEntity).
        builder.HasQueryFilter(t => !t.IsDeleted);
    }
}
```

### 3 — Application: DTOs, command, validator, handler

Create the following under `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Features/Tickets/Commands/CreateTicket/` (mirror whatever folder pattern the customers feature adopted — if that feature used a flatter layout, match it here):

- `CreateTicketCommand.cs`
- `CreateTicketCommandValidator.cs`
- `CreateTicketCommandHandler.cs`
- `CreateTicketResponse.cs` (or reuse a shared `TicketDto`)

Suggested shapes:

```csharp
public record CreateTicketCommand(
    string Subject,
    string? Description,
    Guid CustomerId);

public record CreateTicketResponse(
    Guid Id,
    string Subject,
    string? Description,
    TicketStatus Status,
    Guid CustomerId,
    DateTime CreatedAt);
```

Validator (FluentValidation):

- `Subject`: `NotEmpty`, `MaximumLength(200)`.
- `Description`: `MaximumLength(4000)` when provided.
- `CustomerId`: `NotEmpty` (non-`Guid.Empty`).
- Async rule: `CustomerId` must exist via the customer repository (`ExistsAsync(c => c.Id == command.CustomerId)`). If the customers feature has not yet shipped a repository, defer this check to the handler (see below) and mark it TODO in the validator.

Handler:

1. Verify customer exists (throw `NotFoundException("Customer", command.CustomerId)` if not — the message key comes from `SharedResource.resx`).
2. Instantiate `Ticket { Subject, Description, CustomerId, Status = TicketStatus.New }`.
3. `await _ticketRepository.AddAsync(entity, cancellationToken);`
4. **Call `ITicketHistoryWriter.AppendAsync`** (injected into the handler) to record the ticket creation:
   ```csharp
   await _historyWriter.AppendAsync(
       entity.Id,
       TicketHistoryEventType.Created,
       oldValue: null,
       newValue: $"{entity.Subject}|{entity.CustomerId}",
       note: entity.Description,
       cancellationToken);
   ```
   (This ensures the ticket history timeline has a "Created" entry. The writer will be introduced by `tickets/view-ticket-history`; if that story has not yet landed, inject it as optional and guard with `if (_historyWriter != null)` — update the guard once history lands.)
5. `await _unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);`
6. Map to `CreateTicketResponse` (AutoMapper profile under `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Mappings/`, or inline projection — follow the convention set by the customers feature).
7. Return the response (wrapped in `Result<T>` if that is the established return type — check `Common/Models/Result.cs` and mirror).

Register the new validator and handler in `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/DependencyInjection.cs` **only if** the existing `AddApplication` does not already assembly-scan them.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Missing `Subject`** → 400 with validation error keyed `Ticket.Subject.Required`. Enforced in `CreateTicketCommandValidator`.
- **Subject or description over max length** → 400 with `MaximumLength` validation error. Enforced in validator; DB column length in `TicketConfiguration` acts as the second line of defense.
- **`CustomerId == Guid.Empty`** → 400 via validator `NotEmpty`.
- **`CustomerId` refers to a non-existent or soft-deleted customer** → 404 `NotFoundException("Customer", id)`. Global filter on `Customer.IsDeleted` naturally excludes soft-deleted rows.
- **Unauthenticated caller** → 401 from JWT middleware (`JwtAuthenticationExtensions.cs`).
- **Authenticated caller without an allowed role (e.g. plain Customer role)** → 403 from `[Authorize(Roles = ...)]`.
- **Unicode subject/description (Arabic, emoji)** → must persist unchanged. `nvarchar` columns in SQL Server handle this natively; add an integration test with Arabic input to guard against implicit ASCII conversions.
- **Concurrent creates for the same customer** → both must succeed; there is no uniqueness constraint on ticket subject. Verify no accidental unique index was added in `TicketConfiguration`.
- **Save-changes failure after `AddAsync`** → `IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync` throws; `GlobalExceptionHandler` (`src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Middlewares/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs`) maps to a 500. Do not swallow.
- **Trailing/leading whitespace in `Subject`** → intake does not specify. Default: **do not** trim; validate as-is. Document in a code comment so a later story can revisit.
- **Half-applied migration state** (`AddTickets` runs but app code not yet deployed) → the new table is unused but harmless. See Migration / Rollback below.
- **Customers feature not yet shipped when this story is executed** → executor must stop and coordinate; a `Ticket` referencing a non-existent `Customer` table cannot be created safely. This is called out in Prerequisites.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** `dotnet ef database update` applies `AddTickets`.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef database update <PreviousMigrationName>` removes the `Tickets` table. Because no other feature depends on `Tickets` yet, rollback is safe.
- **Half-applied risk:** if the migration is applied to production but the new API code is not yet deployed, the `Tickets` table sits empty — no user impact. Reverse case (API deployed, migration not applied) surfaces as a SQL exception on the first `POST /api/tickets`; deploy order should be **migration first**.
